data.executive_summary:
# Executive Summary

Imagur operates a public image-sharing website at **imagesharer.xyz** (shown to visitors as **Imager**). This report covers an authorized security assessment of that website and its approved server, performed on **5 October 2026** with the owner's permission.

## Overall result

The assessment confirmed **12 findings**. In the source write-up they were rated **1 critical**, **2 high**, **6 medium**, **1 low**, and **2 informational**. This report keeps those original CVSS vectors. The findings list therefore scores some items differently (cloud keys in public JavaScript score as critical; the open S3 bucket scores as high; PostgreSQL with no scored confidentiality, integrity, or availability impact scores as informational).

The most urgent business issue remains that uploaded files live in an Amazon S3 bucket that anyone on the internet can list and download from. Images the website treats as private are still readable directly from storage.

## What this means for the business

* **Private images are not private in storage.** The site's private setting does not stop a direct download from the storage bucket.
* **One signed-in user can plant files in another user's library** by changing a hidden form field on the upload page.
* **Cloud access keys are in a public JavaScript file** that anyone can download. Those keys were not used against Amazon APIs during this assessment, so whether they still work was not proven. They should still be removed from the site and rotated.
* **The server is open more than it needs to be.** Recursive DNS, PostgreSQL, and a cleartext copy of the login application on port 8080 are reachable from the internet.

## Highest-priority actions

1. Lock the S3 bucket so the public cannot list or download objects. Serve files only through short-lived signed links or the application.
2. Rotate and disable the exposed cloud keys, and remove them from frontend code.
3. Bind uploads to the logged-in user. Ignore any client-supplied user ID.
4. Close PostgreSQL, recursive DNS, and HTTP port 8080 from the internet.

The remaining medium, low, and informational items (session-cookie flags, missing CSRF tokens, missing HSTS/CSP, HTML encoding of filenames, and service banners) should be fixed in the next hardening cycle.

data.scope:
This assessment covered only owner-approved, in-scope assets for Imagur. Testing was performed on 5 October 2026 after authorization was verified on the main public website.

**In-scope (owner approved)**

| System | Description |
|:---|:---|
| imagesharer.xyz | Root domain of the image-sharing site |
| https://imagesharer.xyz/ | Public HTTPS application (branded Imager) |
| 51.161.131.44 | OVH VPS hosting the site (this IP only) |

**Observed during testing, not a separately approved scan target**

Amazon S3 bucket `filesharer-research` (region ap-southeast-2) is used by the in-scope application to store uploaded images. It is mentioned in findings because the approved website writes objects there. Other customers' objects were not downloaded.

**Enumerated but owner-declined / out of scope**

* www.imagesharer.xyz
* resources.imagesharer.xyz
* imagur.xyz
* fshare.xyz
* OVH ASN/netblocks except 51.161.131.44
* CloudFront, Spaceship DNS, Flinders University, Google CDN

**Allowed methods**

Authorization check, passive and low-impact enumeration, owner validation of assets, port discovery on 51.161.131.44, version scan of open ports, web mapping, authenticated testing with tester-created accounts, and safe injection proofs only.

**Forbidden methods (not used)**

Brute force, denial of service, malware, phishing, credential stuffing, password spraying, MFA bypass, lateral movement, destructive changes, and downloading other customers' S3 objects.
data.provided_users: Authenticated testing used tester-created accounts registered through the public website. No owner-provided staff credentials were used. Account passwords, session cookie values, and cloud secret keys are not included in this report.

appendix_sections.title: Methodology
appendix_sections.content:
The assessment followed a phased, non-destructive methodology:

1. Authorization GET to the main public website before any testing.
2. Passive and low-impact enumeration of company-related assets.
3. Owner validation of in-scope versus excluded assets.
4. Port discovery on 51.161.131.44, then version detection on open ports only.
5. Web mapping of login, register, dashboard, profile, image upload, image pages, and common path checks.
6. Authenticated testing with tester-created accounts.
7. Safe injection proofs only. No brute force, denial of service, or data dump of other customers' S3 objects.

Enumeration run timestamps were recorded around 2026-10-04T23:30Z to 2026-10-04T23:37Z. Authorization and assessment are dated 2026-10-05.

appendix_sections.title: Limitations
appendix_sections.content:
The following limitations apply to this assessment:

* www.imagesharer.xyz and resources.imagesharer.xyz were not tested (owner declined).
* No password guessing was performed.
* The AWS IAM key found in public JavaScript was not used against AWS APIs, so key validity is unproven.
* Other S3 objects were not downloaded (only a listing count and our own test objects).
* The PostgreSQL password was not attacked.
* No phone number was available for the business contact record.
* Testing was performed from a single vantage point.

appendix_sections.title: Coverage
appendix_sections.content:
Host 51.161.131.44 ports reviewed:

* 22/tcp — SSH
* 53/tcp — DNS
* 80/tcp — HTTP
* 443/tcp — HTTPS
* 5432/tcp — PostgreSQL
* 8080/tcp — HTTP (Apache/PHP login application)

Web application coverage on https://imagesharer.xyz/:

* login, register, dashboard, profile, image upload, image pages, and common path checks

Confirmed findings in this report: 12 (1 critical, 2 high, 6 medium, 1 low, 2 informational).
